statement_en: Let $\epsilon>0$. Is there some $r\ll_\epsilon 1$ such that the density of integers of the form $2^k+n$, where $k\geq 0$ and $n$ has at most $r$ prime divisors, is at least $1-\epsilon$?

namespace Set
open Filter
open scoped Topology
@[inline]
noncomputable abbrev partialDensity {β : Type*} [Preorder β] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β]
    (S : Set β) (A : Set β := Set.univ) (b : β) : ℝ :=
  ((S ∩ A) ∩ Iio b).ncard / (A ∩ Iio b).ncard
end Set

namespace Set
open Filter
open scoped Topology
noncomputable def lowerDensity {β : Type*} [Preorder β] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot β]
    (S : Set β) (A : Set β := Set.univ) : ℝ :=
  atTop.liminf fun (b : β) ↦ S.partialDensity A b
end Set

def TwoPowAddSet (r : ℕ) := {(2 ^ k + n) | (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ) (_ : n.primeFactors.card ≤ r)}

theorem erdos_97932 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) :
    ∃ r,
    1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity := by
  sorry
